svg.title: DNA problems and repair responses
svg.desc: A terminal mismatch can be proofread. MMR processes escaped mismatches on the new strand. BER removes small base lesions; an AP site is then processed. Human NER excises an oligonucleotide containing a bulky UV lesion. Telomere extension uses telomerase for the G strand and CST Pol alpha primase for C strand fill-in.
svg.text: DNA maintenance: start with the problem
1 Wrong nucleotide at the growing 3′ end
Pol III uses its ε subunit; Pol α has no intrinsic proofreading.
MMR: identify new strand → remove tract → resynthesize
A tumor MMR defect alone does not diagnose inherited Lynch syndrome.
BER: base removal → AP-site processing → fill → seal
An already-existing AP site skips the initial glycosylase step.
4 Bulky UV lesion in human DNA
NER: open region → dual incision → replace oligonucleotide
Bypassing a lesion with a polymerase is not the same as removing it.
Telomerase: existing DNA 3′-OH + internal RNA template
→ extend G strand; CST–Pol α–primase fills C strand
Telomere maintenance supports proliferation; it does not alone cause cancer.
